compiled_state.title: reconciler dedup test: pre-existing dso-id -> mapping.json not written, FakeAcliClient lacks get_comments
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 0f51601b96b54078a474f639dc8dfec3e58e7d99
* **test:** tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_e2e_dedup_pass.py::test_pre_existing_dso_id_produces_zero_creates

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (pre-existing failure discovered during bug 8b25 parent-sync work)

#### Expected Behavior

The dedup guard, on encountering a pre-existing dso-id label match, must write bridge_state/mapping.json atomically (per the dedup-create-skipped contract in applier.create_one). Test asserts the file exists.

#### Actual Behavior

Test fails at line 207: \"mapping.json must be written by the dedup guard\" — PosixPath(.../bridge_state/mapping.json).exists() is False. Captured stderr shows: WARNING: inbound_create: get_comments for 'uuid-X' failed (AttributeError(\"'FakeAcliClient' object has no attribute 'get_comments'\")). The inbound_create comment-bootstrap path raises on the test's FakeAcliClient, which lacks a get_comments method; the dedup/mapping write is short-circuited.

attribution_basis: evidenced — fails identically on parent commit 0f51601b96 with the working tree stashed (confirmed via git stash + targeted pytest run). Independent of bug 8b25's inbound_differ change.

This is the project baseline's known 1 failing test (792/1/2). Filing per CLAUDE.md always:tracking-issues.

comments.body: CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-05, investigation): The ticket diagnosis ("test-harness gap — add a get_comments stub to FakeAcliClient") is a RED HERRING and does NOT fix the failure. Verified on HEAD: (1) applier._apply_inbound_create now wraps client.get_comments in try/except Exception (applier.py:843-857), so the AttributeError is CAUGHT and logged as a warning — it is a symptom, not the cause. (2) After adding a get_comments()->[] stub the test STILL FAILS: mapping.json is never written. REAL ROOT CAUSE: a brand-new key diffs to a typed Mutation(direction=inbound, action=create, target=uuid-X, local_id=None) (differ.py:447) and routes to _apply_inbound_create, which — unlike the outbound create_one (applier.py:2004-2029) — has NO dedup guard: it never searches for a pre-existing dso-id:<id> label, never writes bridge_state/mapping.json, and never emits the dedup-create-skipped manifest event the test asserts (test docstring + assertions 3b/3c). So this is a PRODUCTION defect (missing inbound-create dedup symmetry), not a test gap. NUANCE/RISK before fixing: the test keys the dedup on the mutation TARGET (uuid-X) — search dso-id:uuid-X, mapping[uuid-X]=PROJ-999 — but for a real inbound create target is a Jira key (e.g. DIG-1234), and dso-id labels store the LOCAL id, so dso-id:<jira-key> would not normally match; the correct inbound dedup key/semantics need a deciding call. Also: mirroring create_one adds one Jira search per inbound create (perf: f6cc comment #8 notes ~2050 inbound creates in prod). Recommended fix: add an inbound dedup guard mirroring create_one (skip-create + _write_mapping_atomic + dedup-create-skipped event), with the dedup key resolved correctly for production inbound semantics. Dedup candidates b38a/38fd/4cc1 share this exact defect; 4cc1 ALSO carries a separate order-dependent flaky test (test_fetcher_dedup_observable.py::test_dedup_suppression_emits_alert) — distinct issue.
